issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting requirements for the Farm.animals collection: the UML diagram shows animals: List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 explicitly requires using a Set implemented as a HashSet (unique animals, initialize HashSet in no-arg constructor). The provided solution uses a List (ArrayList) for the animals attribute and initializes it as an ArrayList. This mismatch between UML, textual specification, and solution threatens student understanding (which collection type to implement) and may cause tests or instructor expectations to disagree with student implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) update the problem statement (text and UML) to require a List/ArrayList and remove the uniqueness/HashSet requirement; or (B) update the solution and any template code to use a Set<Animal> (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals; initialized as new HashSet<>(); with getter/setter using Set) so it matches the textual instruction about unique animals. Also ensure the UML and textual description agree.
